title: Synthesis and mastery
goal: Done when you can run the five-layer protocol with a sensitivity rerun on one question, write a falsifiable ledger entry with a confidence and scoring rule, and explain which parts of your own chart survive a change of convention.

convention_profile: The full list of settings that produced a chart: ayanamsa, node type, house system, dasha year length, karaka scheme and matching table set. Every result should be quoted with its profile.
double_transit: A timing filter: a house is activated in a year when both Jupiter and Saturn, by occupation or aspect, reach it by transit. Attribution varies by source; the rule is a teaching framework, not a verified law.
ledger: A dated, locked record of predictions: window, house, falsifiable outcome, confidence, convention profile and sensitivity result. Outcomes are scored later against criteria written in advance.
brier: The average of (confidence minus outcome) squared, where the outcome is 1 if the event happened and 0 if not. Lower is better. Always saying 50% scores 0.25.
base_rate: How often an event happens anyway, for anyone of that age in a window of that length. A prediction is only informative if it beats this.
hindsight: After an outcome is known, people remember having expected it. Locked, timestamped entries are the remedy.
sensitivity: Repeating a reading under a second ayanamsa, the other node type, another dasha year length and a birth time a few minutes either side, then reporting whether the answer holds.

lessons.title: The five-layer cross-check protocol
lessons.body:
Recall: Why does agreement between KP, Tajika and Yogini prove less than it seems to, on your chart?

One question, five layers

Never answer a life question from one technique. Run it through five layers in order and show each result separately. The layers are a design built from documented practice. No school publishes a rule for settling a disagreement between them.

LayerQuestionChecks
1 PromiseCan this happen in this life?House, lord and varga for the matter; yogas; Ashtakavarga bindus
2 WindowWhen is it activated?Vimshottari mahadasha and antardasha; a second dasha (Chara or Yogini)
3 TriggerWhich year or months?{{term:double_transit|Double transit}} of Jupiter and Saturn; optional Tajika annual chart
4 Binary checkYes or no?KP cuspal sub lord signification
5 SensitivityDoes the answer survive uncertainty?Second ayanamsa, other node, dasha year, birth time ±N minutes

All five layers use the same birth time and mostly the same ephemeris. “Four of five agree” overstates confidence if the input is wrong. That is why layer 5 is compulsory.

Worked example

In your chart

Question, written before looking: Is a visible step in work or business likely, and in which window? Houses: 10th (work), 7th (partners, clients), 2nd and 11th (income, gains). Profile: Lahiri, mean node, whole-sign houses, 365.25-day years, Satna.

LayerWhat was checkedResult
1 Promise10th lord Mercury in own sign in the 10th (Bhadra) with the Sun (Budh-Aditya); 7th lord Jupiter in own sign in the 7th (Hamsa); 11th lord Moon in own sign in the 11thFor. Bindus are near average: H10 27, H11 26, H7 29 against a mean of 28.1 (337 ÷ 12). D10 has Jupiter in its lagna in its own sign, but Mercury sits in Pisces, its fall sign. The engine also lists Kendradhipati dosha for Mercury and Jupiter. Mixed
2 WindowMercury–Saturn to 29 Sep 2027, Ketu–Ketu to 25 Feb 2028, Ketu–Venus 25 Feb 2028 to 27 Apr 2029. Venus rules the 2nd and 9th and sits in the 9th in its own signKetu–Venus is the best fit. Yogini (Sankata, 2022 to 2030) and Chara (Aquarius, 2025 to 2031) are too long to discriminate
3 TriggerJupiter and Saturn both occupying or aspecting Gemini (10th), by sign, from the dates computed with Swiss Ephemeris10th: 27 Dec 2028 to 29 Mar 2029, and 6 Oct 2029 to 24 Jan 2030. The first falls inside Ketu–Venus. The 7th (Pisces): 25 Jan to 2 Jun 2027 and 27 Nov 2027 to 23 Feb 2028, the second inside Ketu–Ketu
4 BinaryKP 10th cusp sub lord Saturn signifies 5, 6, 7; 11th Mars signifies 3, 8, 9; 7th Sun signifies 9, 11, 12Partial for the 10th, none for the 11th, mixed for the 7th. KP tests the promise here, not the date
5 SensitivityReruns in lesson 12-2Window flips under Raman ayanamsa and shifts by months under a 360-day year. KP 10th sub lord holds for birth times 12:58 to 13:06

Agreement count: promise mostly for; window, trigger and binary each partial or yes; sensitivity fails under two conventions. The honest entry is therefore “possible step in the 10th house, 27 Dec 2028 to 29 Mar 2029, low-to-moderate confidence, flips under Raman.” The transit windows were not rerun under other ayanamsas, so their stability is untested.

Where the schools differ

Double transit. Attribution varies: K.N. Rao is the name most often given, and some sources credit B.V. Raman. It is a modern teaching framework, not a rule stated in BPHS. Teaching pages list Jupiter aspects differently, and some count only aspect, not occupation. This lesson counts Jupiter on its 5th, 7th and 9th and Saturn on its 3rd, 7th and 10th, and counts occupation for both.

Varga choice. P.V.R. Narasimha Rao advises using the divisional chart specific to the matter (D10 for work, D4 for property). K.N. Rao’s composite approach runs several dashas side by side.

Cross-check

Run a negative control: apply the same five layers to a question where your chart gives no promise, and see how often they still return “yes.” If the protocol says yes to everything, it is not discriminating.

Remember
  • Order: promise, window, trigger, binary check, sensitivity.
  • Show each layer’s result and its convention. Never blend them into one verdict.
  • Agreement among layers is limited by shared inputs, so sensitivity is mandatory.
  • The output is a dated, falsifiable entry with a confidence, not a prophecy.

Practice: Pick one question about 2027 or 2028 that matters to you. Fill the five-layer table for it in your notes. State the agreement count and one sensitivity flip. Do not write a verdict stronger than the table supports.
lessons.listen: The five-layer protocol runs one question through promise, window, trigger, a binary check and a sensitivity rerun, and shows each result separately. Promise asks whether the chart can support the event at all. Window uses the dasha. Trigger uses the double transit of Jupiter and Saturn. The binary check uses the KP cuspal sub lord. Sensitivity reruns the answer under other settings. All of these share your birth time, so agreement overstates confidence. On your chart, asking about a visible step in work gives a mostly favourable promise, with Mercury, Jupiter and the Moon in their own signs. Ketu–Venus from February 2028 is the best dasha fit, and the tenth house gets a double transit from 27 December 2028 to 29 March 2029. KP gives a partial yes. The window flips under the Raman ayanamsa. So the honest entry is a possible step, with low to moderate confidence.
sources: Project research notes, “Jyotish learning app gaps”: five-layer table and the statement that it is a design from documented practice, not a standard
B.V. Raman, double transit, as credited by the source consulted (unconfirmed attribution to K.N. Rao)
P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, 2014 article on dasha and transit, as cited in the research notes
Engine output and Swiss Ephemeris scripts in /home/claude/jyotish-path/work for the chart facts

quiz.q: What is the correct order of the five layers?
o: Promise, window, trigger, binary check, sensitivity
quiz.w: The chart must hold the promise first, then the dasha opens the window, then transits pick the time.

quiz.q: Why is the sensitivity layer compulsory?
o: The other layers share the same inputs, so agreement can hide a wrong birth time or setting
quiz.w: Shared inputs mean shared errors.

quiz.q: In your worked example, which dasha period overlaps the 10th-house double transit of 27 Dec 2028 to 29 Mar 2029?
quiz.w: Ketu–Venus runs 25 Feb 2028 to 27 Apr 2029.

quiz.q: What does a negative control test?
o: Whether the protocol says yes even where the chart gives no promise
quiz.w: A protocol that always says yes is not discriminating.

lessons.title: Convention profiles and sensitivity reruns
lessons.body:
Recall: Name the five layers and say which one is never optional.

The profile is part of the answer

A {{term:convention_profile|convention profile}} lists every setting behind a result: ayanamsa, node type, house system, dasha year length, karaka scheme. A reading without its profile cannot be checked. A {{term:sensitivity|sensitivity rerun}} changes one setting at a time and reports what moves.

SettingCommon choicesMoves
AyanamsaLahiri; Krishnamurti (about 6′ lower); Raman (about 1.4° lower); Yukteshwar (about 1.4° lower)Planet signs, nakshatras, every dasha date
NodeMean or trueRahu and Ketu by up to about 1.7°
Dasha year365.25 days (most software) or 360Every dasha date; a Saturn mahadasha by about 100 days
Birth timeRecorded time ±N minutesLagna, KP cusps, navamsa, dasha dates slightly
HousesWhole-sign, equal, Placidus (KP)House numbers, not signs
In your chart

Your chart (12:59 IST, Satna) rerun one setting at a time. Lahiri values are from the engine; the other rows are from a Swiss Ephemeris script.

RunLagnaMoonMarsMercury to Ketu mahadasha
Lahiri, 365.25-dayVirgo 21°52′Cancer 8°04′ PushyaTaurus 29°19′29 Sep 2027
Krishnamurti ayanamsaVirgo 21°58′Cancer 8°10′ PushyaTaurus 29°25′10 Aug 2027
Raman ayanamsaVirgo 23°19′Cancer 9°31′ PushyaGemini 0°46′about Sep 2025
Yukteshwar ayanamsaVirgo 23°15′Cancer 9°26′ PushyaGemini 0°42′about Oct 2025
Lahiri, 360-day yearVirgo 21°52′Cancer 8°04′ PushyaTaurus 29°19′28 Apr 2027
Birth time −5 minVirgo 20°44′Cancer 8°01′ Pushya23 Oct 2027
Birth time +5 minVirgo 23°00′Cancer 8°07′ Pushya5 Sep 2027

Stable: Virgo lagna and the Moon in Cancer in Pushya hold across all runs.

Flips: under Raman or Yukteshwar, Mars moves from Taurus (9th) to Gemini (10th), and the Ketu mahadasha would already have started in late 2025. By the same rule you used in Stage 9, ranking by degree within the sign, Mercury at 29°37′ would then top the list and Mars at 0°46′ would fall to the bottom, so the Atmakaraka changes from Mars to Mercury. Your Jaimini reading is therefore tied to Lahiri.

Shifts: ±5 minutes moves the Ketu mahadasha by about three to four weeks; a 360-day year moves it by five months.

Node: mean Rahu is Leo 10°33′ and true Rahu is Leo 9°09′. Both stay in Leo.

Boundary warnings

ItemMarginWhy it matters
Mars, Taurus 29°19′41′ from GeminiA sign change under other ayanamsas; Mars is also combust
Mercury, Gemini 28°10′1°50′ from CancerClose, but no sign change under the ayanamsas tested
Jupiter, Pisces 3°28′8′ past the Purva Bhadrapada edgeAn ayanamsa about 8′ larger than Lahiri puts Jupiter in a different nakshatra and a different nakshatra lord
Venus, Taurus 8°18′1°42′ from the end of KrittikaSafe under the ayanamsas tested
Where the schools differ

Which profile is “right”? Lahiri is the Indian government standard and the default in most software. Raman and Yukteshwar have their own followers. The Krishnamurti ayanamsa is used with KP. No test settles it, so report your profile every time and prefer conclusions that survive several.

Cross-check

Check any reading you plan to log by rerunning it under Krishnamurti ayanamsa (small shift), a 360-day year (dasha shift) and ±5 minutes (birth time). If it flips under a small shift, write it as low confidence. If it flips only under a far-off ayanamsa, say so and keep the main profile.

Remember
  • Always quote the profile.
  • Change one setting at a time and note what moves.
  • Your Virgo lagna and Pushya Moon are stable. Mars sign, AK and the dasha clock are not.
  • Boundary warnings come first: Mars (41′ from a sign edge) and Jupiter (8′ past a nakshatra edge).

Practice: Take your own 2027 question from the last lesson and rerun the window layer under Krishnamurti ayanamsa and a 360-day year. Which dates move and by how much?
lessons.listen: A convention profile lists every setting that produced a result: ayanamsa, node type, house system, dasha year length and karaka scheme. A sensitivity rerun changes one setting at a time and reports what moves. On your chart the Virgo lagna and the Moon in Pushya in Cancer hold under all runs. Mars does not. At twenty-nine degrees nineteen minutes of Taurus it sits forty-one minutes from Gemini, and under the Raman or Yukteshwar ayanamsa it moves into Gemini, which changes the house, and by the degree rule changes your Atmakaraka from Mars to Mercury. The Mercury to Ketu change is twenty-ninth September 2027 under Lahiri, about three to four weeks either side for five minutes of birth-time error, tenth August 2027 under the Krishnamurti ayanamsa, and twenty-eighth April 2027 with a 360-day year. Prefer conclusions that survive several profiles.
sources: Project research notes: ayanamsa offsets, dasha year length, node differences and the boundary-warning design
Engine natal and dasha output for the Lahiri rows; Swiss Ephemeris script calc17.py and calc20.py in /home/claude/jyotish-path/work for the other rows

quiz.q: Under which setting does your Mars change sign?
quiz.w: Under Raman (and Yukteshwar) Mars moves to Gemini 0°46′.

quiz.q: What happens to the Atmakaraka under Raman ayanamsa by the degree-ranking rule?
quiz.w: Mercury at 29°37′ ranks highest.

quiz.q: Which of these is stable across every run in the table?
o: Virgo lagna and the Moon in Pushya
quiz.w: Lagna sign and the Moon’s nakshatra do not change.

quiz.q: By how much does a 360-day year move your Mercury to Ketu change, compared with Lahiri 365.25?
quiz.w: It moves from 29 Sep 2027 to 28 Apr 2027.

lessons.title: Writing and scoring predictions: the ledger, base rates and hindsight
lessons.body:
Recall: Which of your chart facts changes under the Raman ayanamsa, and which does not?

What a good prediction looks like

A prediction you cannot be wrong about teaches nothing. Each {{term:ledger|ledger}} entry needs these fields, and they are locked before the event.

FieldRule
Date written and profileTimestamp it; store the convention profile
WindowStart and end dates. Windows over about two years, or spread across many houses, are low-falsifiability
House and areaOne primary house; list secondary ones
Outcome statementObservable and dated: “I sign X”, not “I feel more stable”
ConfidenceA number from 0 to 100%, chosen before the event
Layers agreeing and sensitivityFrom the five-layer table
Base rateHow often it happens anyway in a window this long
Scoring ruleWritten in advance: what counts as a hit

Scoring honestly

  • Base rate. {{term:base_rate|Base rate}} is how often the event happens anyway. If a job change happens in about one year in five for people of your age, a prediction of “job change in 2028” has to beat that, and the 20% figure here is only an example, not a statistic.
  • Brier score. The {{term:brier|Brier score}} averages (confidence − outcome)². Illustration: confidences 0.8 (hit), 0.6 (miss), 0.7 (hit) give (0.04 + 0.36 + 0.09) ÷ 3 = 0.163. Always saying 0.5 gives 0.25. Lower than 0.25 over many entries means your confidence has information in it.
  • Hindsight. {{term:hindsight|Hindsight bias}} (described by Baruch Fischhoff in 1975) makes people remember they expected what happened. Lock entries and never edit them.
  • Vague statements. Statements that fit almost anyone feel personal (the Forer effect, 1949). Ask: would this sentence fit a random person of my age?
In your chart

A base rate you can compute from your own dasha dates. Between 1 Jan 2013 and 27 Nov 2026 (about 167 months) your engine shows 8 antardasha boundaries: 25 Feb 2013, 22 Feb 2014, 23 Dec 2016, 29 Oct 2017, 31 Mar 2019, 27 Mar 2020, 14 Oct 2022 and 19 Jan 2025. A “within three months of a boundary” window covers 6 months around each, so 8 × 6 = 48 of 167 months, about 28 to 29% (the first window starts before 1 Jan 2013). A random life event therefore falls near an antardasha change about three times in ten without any astrology. Hitting that window is weak evidence.

FieldEntry 1 (format example; you set the confidence)
Written27 Nov 2026; Lahiri, mean node, whole-sign, 365.25-day, Satna
Window27 Dec 2028 to 29 Mar 2029 (3 months)
House and area10th (work); 2nd (income) shares the same double transit
OutcomeA new role, venture or formal responsibility in my main work begins, with a dated start I can show
LayersPromise mostly for; window partial (Ketu–Venus); trigger yes; binary partial; sensitivity flips under Raman and 360-day year
Base rateEstimate for a 3-month window; if you do not know it, say so
ScoringHit only if the start date falls inside the window
Cross-check

Ask a sceptical friend for the same question without showing your chart. If they can produce an equally specific window by guessing, the chart has added nothing for that question.

Blind tests of astrologers (Carlson 1985; Narlikar et al. 2009) are why this stage measures outcomes instead of trusting confidence.

Remember
  • Write before the event; lock it; score only by pre-set rules.
  • A window over two years or across many houses is low-falsifiability.
  • Compare every hit with the base rate.
  • The Brier score rewards honest confidence: 0.25 is the always-50% baseline.

Practice: Write your first three ledger entries, each with a window of under a year, a measurable outcome, a confidence and a scoring rule. Email them to yourself so they carry a timestamp.
lessons.listen: A useful prediction is dated, observable and locked before the event. Each ledger entry records the convention profile, a window, one primary house, an outcome you could show to a stranger, a confidence number, which layers agreed, how it behaved under sensitivity reruns, and the base rate. The base rate is how often the event happens anyway. On your own dasha dates, eight antardasha boundaries between 2013 and late 2026 mean that about twenty-eight to twenty-nine per cent of random dates fall within three months of a boundary, so hitting such a window proves little. The Brier score averages the squared gap between your confidence and the outcome, and always saying fifty per cent scores a quarter. Hindsight bias makes you remember expecting what happened, so lock every entry, and ask whether a sentence would fit a random person of your age.
sources: Project research notes: prediction ledger design (entries locked before events, windows over about two years flagged, hit rate shown beside a base rate); the notes did not source forecasting-calibration literature
Brier score as a standard scoring rule; Fischhoff (1975) on hindsight bias; Forer (1949) on subjective validation, cited from general knowledge, not from the project notes
Engine dasha output for the boundary count

quiz.q: Which entry is falsifiable?
o: “A new role starts between 27 Dec 2028 and 29 Mar 2029, with a dated start”
quiz.w: It has a window, an observable outcome and a scoring rule.

quiz.q: What does a Brier score of 0.25 from always answering 50% tell you?
o: It is the baseline to beat
It means the prediction was wrong
quiz.w: Lower than 0.25 over many entries shows your confidence carries information.

quiz.q: What fraction of random dates falls within 3 months of one of your recent antardasha boundaries?
quiz.w: 8 boundaries × 6 months ÷ about 167 months.

quiz.q: Why lock entries?
quiz.w: Locking prevents you from remembering you expected what happened.

lessons.title: Client communication and ethics
lessons.body:
Recall: Which two fields in a ledger entry guard against vague and flattering statements?

How to speak

You may read charts for family or friends or, later, for clients. These rules apply from the first reading.

SituationSayDo not say
Stating a prediction“Traditional Jyotish indicates … in this window; I give it 40% and will log it.”“This will happen.” “100% accurate.”
A hard placementWhat the house signifies, what helps, what schools disagree on“You are cursed.” “Danger.” “Doomed.”
TimingA window with a start and end, and its sensitivityA single exact date, unless the birth time is verified
Asked for remediesPractical actions: sleep, savings, written contracts, documented decisions. Devotional practice only as an optional, labelled choiceGemstones or rituals sold as fixes
Asked “should I?”Show the chart view, then say the decision needs facts and a professional where relevantMaking a decision for them

Consent and privacy

  • Birth details tied to a named person are personal data. India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 applies to such data. Its Rules were notified in November 2025, with obligations phased in over about 18 months, so check the current position and take legal advice before running this as a service.
  • Read another person’s chart only with their consent. Never read a partner’s, employee’s or rival’s chart in secret.
  • For a minor, involve a parent or guardian. Do not make predictions about a child’s health, marriage or fate.
  • Store birth data only as long as needed. Do not share a chart or reading without permission.
  • Do not tie fees to outcomes.

When to refer

SignalRefer to
Symptoms, pain, medication, a diagnosisA doctor. Wellness timing is not diagnosis
Hopelessness, self-harm talk, abuseEmergency or crisis services, immediately (in India, the Tele-MANAS helpline is 14416). Stop the reading
Contracts, disputes, property or family lawA lawyer
Investments, loans, insurance, taxA licensed financial or tax professional
Anxiety that the chart is causingStop reading. Offer a calmer, practical frame, and suggest a counsellor if it persists
In your chart

Your chart has real-looking “bad” placements, and the engine output lets you practise rewriting them. Saturn is in Aries, its fall sign, in the 8th house.

Fear versionHonest version
“Debilitated Saturn in the 8th brings sudden losses.”“Saturn is in its fall sign in the 8th house. The engine lists two cancellation candidates (Saturn in a kendra from the Moon; the Sun in a kendra from the lagna) and a Harsha viparita yoga (6th lord in the 8th). Schools differ on how much cancellation counts. The 8th concerns shared resources, risk and hidden matters. Practical: keep cash reserves, put agreements in writing, review insurance with a licensed professional.”

The honest version states the fact, names the variants, then gives actions. It contains no fear and no promise.

Where the schools differ

Where practice differs. Many traditional practitioners prescribe gemstones and rituals as standard. This course’s rule is stricter: no selling of remedies, only labelled optional practices. No controlled test known to this course shows that traditional remedies work. Do not claim they do.

Cross-check

Test any sentence you plan to say: remove the astrology words and see if you would still say it to this person. If the only effect would be fear, drop it. If it names a concrete action, keep it.

Remember
  • Say “traditional Jyotish indicates”, give a window and confidence, and log it.
  • No fear, no guarantees, no remedy selling.
  • Consent first; minors through a parent; data kept minimal.
  • Refer out for medical, legal, financial and mental-health matters.

Practice: Take one placement from your chart that worries you. Write the fear version, then rewrite it in the three parts above: the fact, the variants, and the actions.
lessons.listen: Ethics starts with how you speak. Say that traditional Jyotish indicates something, give a window and a confidence, and log it. Avoid guarantees, fear language and exact dates unless the birth time is verified. Do not sell gemstones or rituals. Offer practical actions, and label any devotional practice as optional. Get consent before reading anyone’s chart, involve a parent or guardian for a minor, keep data minimal, and do not link fees to outcomes. Refer to a doctor for symptoms, to emergency or crisis services for hopelessness or abuse, to a lawyer for legal matters and to a licensed professional for money. Practise on your own chart: Saturn in its fall sign in the eighth house becomes a fact, a note on cancellation variants, and practical steps such as reserves, written agreements and reviewed insurance. Never a curse.
sources: Project instructions and spec: honesty rules (no guarantees, no fear language, no remedy selling) and the ledger design
Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (India) and DPDP Rules, 2025 (notified November 2025, phased over about 18 months; PIB release and law-firm summaries)
Engine natal output for Saturn’s dignity, bhanga candidates and yoga list

quiz.q: A client mentions chest pain and asks if Saturn is the cause. What do you do?
o: Tell them to see a doctor and keep the astrology out of the diagnosis
quiz.w: Wellness timing is not diagnosis; refer.

quiz.q: Which wording follows the course rules?
o: “Traditional Jyotish indicates a window of Jan to Mar 2029 for X; I give it 40% and I will log it.”
“Wear this stone and it will pass.”
quiz.w: Window, confidence, ledger.

quiz.q: When may you read someone else’s chart?
quiz.w: Consent comes first.

quiz.q: What are the three parts of an honest rewrite of a hard placement?
quiz.w: State the fact, show where schools differ, give actions.

lessons.title: A blind case exercise
lessons.body:
Recall: What is the Brier score of someone who always answers 50%?

Why you need a blind test

Reading a chart when you already know the life is not a test. You will find the fit. A blind exercise removes what you know and counts hits against chance. It is the only way to learn whether your reading adds anything.

The protocol

  1. Sealer. A second person picks a consenting subject with a reliably recorded birth time. The sealer writes down 4 to 6 dated life events from the past and two things that did not happen in the period, and seals them.
  2. Questions. The sealer gives you only the birth data and the questions, for example “in which year between 2015 and 2024 did the first major job change happen?”.
  3. Reader (you). Fix the convention profile. Use the five layers for each question. Write a window of a year or less and a confidence, then lock the entry.
  4. Unseal. Score each question against the window, using the scoring rule written first.
  5. Compare with chance. A one-year window in a ten-year span has a 10% chance of hitting by luck.
Illustration only (invented numbers)Value
Span10 years
Window per question1 year, so chance = 10%
Questions5
Hits2
Chance of 2 or more hits by luckabout 8% (1 − 0.9⁵ − 5 × 0.1 × 0.9⁴ = 0.081)

Even 2 hits in 5 is not strong evidence. A real test needs dozens of entries, and the result should be reported whatever it shows.

In your chart

Your own chart is a poor blind subject for the past, because you know the answers. Use it as a forward test instead: write entries now and let outcomes arrive. The engine gives dated checkpoints in 2027 to anchor the entries.

DateEvent (engine)Entry to write before it
3 Jun 2027Saturn enters AriesTrigger entry for the 7th house window (25 Jan to 2 Jun 2027 ends here)
26 Jun 2027Jupiter enters LeoEntry for 12th-house themes (expenses, distance, rest)
29 Sep 2027Mercury–Saturn ends, Ketu beginsDasha-change entry (range 10 Aug to 23 Oct 2027 across the reruns)

Entries about 2028 and 2029 are also fine; they simply take longer to score. Ask a sealer for a second set from a family member’s chart if you want past events.

Where the schools differ

What astrologers say. After blind tests, astrologers have argued that the testers were not competent or the tasks did not fit the tradition. Critics of the Pune test (Narlikar et al. 2009) made these arguments, and the test has been criticised in turn. The remaining problem is that the tradition has no agreed success criterion set before outcomes. In this exercise you fix that criterion yourself, in advance.

Cross-check

Include a negative control question in every set (one thing that did not happen). If you predict that too, your method is saying yes to everything.

Remember
  • Blind means the reader sees no events until the entries are locked.
  • Compare hits with chance from the window length.
  • Small samples mislead; log everything and report all results.
  • On your own chart use forward entries, since you know your past.

Practice: Ask someone you trust to be a sealer for a family member who consents. Agree the questions, the span and the scoring rule in writing before you see any events.
lessons.listen: A blind exercise removes what you already know. A sealer picks a consenting subject with a recorded birth time, writes four to six dated past events and two that did not happen, and seals them. You get only the birth data and the questions, use the five layers under a fixed convention profile, write windows of a year or less with a confidence, and lock them. Then you unseal and score against the rule written first, and compare with chance. In a ten-year span a one-year window hits by luck ten per cent of the time, so two hits in five questions still happens by luck about eight per cent of the time. You cannot be blind on your own past, so use your chart as a forward test with entries before Saturn enters Aries on third June 2027, Jupiter enters Leo on twenty-sixth June, and the Ketu dasha starts on twenty-ninth September 2027.
sources: Project research notes: description of the Carlson and Narlikar tests, their limits, and the point that the tradition lacks a pre-set success criterion
Engine events output for 2027 ingress dates and dasha output for the Ketu change

quiz.q: Why is your own past a poor blind subject?
o: You know the events, so fit is guaranteed
quiz.w: Knowledge of the events contaminates the reading.

quiz.q: A one-year window in a ten-year span hits by chance how often?
quiz.w: One year out of ten.

quiz.q: What does a negative control do?
o: Shows if the method says yes to everything
quiz.w: It exposes a method that never says no.

quiz.q: Which comes first?
o: Unsealing, then deciding the scoring rule
quiz.w: The scoring rule must be set before the outcome is known.

lessons.title: Capstone: your complete reading, as hypotheses to log
lessons.body:

Everything in one place

Where the schools differ

Where the schools part on this chart. Parashari reads Saturn’s fall in the 8th with its cancellation candidates and Harsha yoga. Jaimini reads Mars as Atmakaraka (7 or 8 karaka schemes agree here at Lahiri). KP reads the cusp sub lords and may call the 7th and 11th unstable. Tajika reads the year, which is undecided. None of them settles the others, and each should be read as its own check.

Cross-check

Before you log, run the five-layer table for each hypothesis, state the agreement count, and write one sensitivity flip per entry. If two entries conflict, report both.

Everything here is a hypothesis to log, not a prediction to rely on. No decision about health, money, contracts or relationships should rest on it.

Remember
  • A complete reading is a list of dated, falsifiable hypotheses with their layers and sensitivity.
  • Your stable facts: Virgo lagna, Pushya Moon. Fragile facts: Mars sign, Atmakaraka and dasha dates under other profiles.
  • Log first, then act on facts and professional advice, not on the hypotheses.
  • Re-read your ledger each quarter and update your confidence from what happened.
